items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with a Territorial Acknowledgement and recognition of the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, as well as October 4, Sisters in Spirit Day, a day to raise awareness about missing and murdered Indigenous women, girls and two-spirit people. Mayor McCabe spoke about the work of a local indigenous artist, and the bus and ambulance wrap they created, telling Artist Bernard-Resmer’s own description of the artwork and what the theme “They are returning home” is speaking to.

As a City, we re-commit ourselves to continued learning about and grappling with the truth during this time of reflection and remembrance. We further commit to the year- round and long-term work of reconciliation with the goal of creating a better community for the seven generations yet to come.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: WRPS Presentation – The Future Use of CCTV in Community Safety
notes: Jen Davis, Deputy Chief, Waterloo Regional Police Services gave a presentation outlining the reasons for Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) and Automatic License Plate Reader (ALPR) use in the community, as well as the reasoning behind the locations of the cameras, how the system would be used, and the capabilities and restrictions of the technology.
Julie Finley-Swaren, City Clerk, City of Waterloo added some information regarding the City’s role in the project, including reviewing privacy concerns.
Jen Davis responded to questions of Council. Julie Finley-Swaren also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Reep Green Solutions
notes: Patrick Gilbride, Executive Director, Reep Green Solutions gave a presentation celebrating 25 years and outlining their Impact Report from 2024-2025, including the things that they have been championing such as heat pumps in homes and tree planting. He then responded to questions of Council.

Ashlyn Fox gave a presentation detailing the proposed development, including site context, the current planning framework, and the Official Plan and Zoning by-law amendments being requested. She then responded to questions of Council. John Vos also responded to questions of Council.

Nicholas Dell, Harper Dell & Associates gave a presentation further outlining the proposed development, including information on Bill 185 regarding the parking, as well as feedback received from staff. Nicholas Dell responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Informal Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Wright noted that we often talk about firekeeping when discussing the First Nations presence in the community. She wanted to draw attention to the All Nations Grand River Water Walk, which just concluded, running from September 21-27.

Waterkeepers are stewards who promote the sacredness of water, safeguard local waters, and they play a really important role in the community, centring watershed issues. Councillor Wright wanted to highlight waterkeepers and the work they have done to raise attention to the Grand River over the last many days.

Councillor Wright also gave a shout out to William Martin, who has been attending the chambers for the past two years, initiating conversations between local First Nations groups and the local institutions. Seeing that no community event was booked in the Waterloo Public Square to recognize the National Day of Truth and Reconciliation, he organized an event in partnership with local First Nations groups and the Waterloo Regional Police Service. It takes place tomorrow, September 30, at 2:00 p.m.

Councillor Roe wanted to bring awareness to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) halting a program tomorrow, September 30, wherein refugees arriving in Canada would be housed in hotels. With housing already precarious for everyone, this adds another burden and barrier on newcomers to Canada.

motions.item_title: Consideration of Notice of Motion Given at Previous Meeting
motions.text: WHEREAS under Ontario Regulation 391/2, Blue Box producers are fully accountable and financially responsible for their products and packaging once they reach their end of life and are disposed of for ‘eligible’ sources only; and WHEREAS ‘ineligible’ sources, which producers are not responsible for, include business improvement areas, places of worship, daycares, campgrounds, public facing and internal areas of municipal-owned buildings, and not-for-profit organizations, such as shelters and food banks; and WHEREAS the province amended Ontario Regulation 391/2 to not expand services for new public space recycling; and WHEREAS should a municipality continue to provide services to the ‘ineligible’ sources, the municipality will be required to oversee the collection, transportation, and processing of the recycling, assuming 100% of the costs; and THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT City of Waterloo Council request that the province amend Ontario Regulation 391/21, Blue Box so that producers are responsible for the end-of-life management of recycling products from all sources as stated above; AND THAT Council request the support of all Ontario Municipalities; AND THAT this resolution be forwarded to the Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, the Honourable Todd McCarthy, Minister of the Environment, Conservation and Parks, the Honourable Mike Harris, Minister of Natural Resources, the Honourable Rob Flack, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, to local and area MPPs, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), the Association of Municipal Managers, Clerks and Treasurers of Ontario (AMCTO), and to the Region of Waterloo and local area municipalities.
